subject: Short-lived audit logs: proposal for granular deletion and SIG evidence
messages:
From: Timothy Rogers <tim.rogers@aurabox.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurabox Legal <legal@aurabox.com>, ops+security@aurabox.com
Date: 2028-05-27T16:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Granular deletion exception for short-lived audit records / SIG artifacts

Hi Jasmine,

Quick note from our compliance team: Aurabox has a customer-specific requirement where certain processing-event audit rows (session-start/end, ephemeral telemetry) must be purged within 7 days, but our internal forensics playbook occasionally needs targeted access for 30 days. The standard Redwood retention for these mini-audit rows is 30 days, and Legal is asking if we can get an exception path that supports granular deletion (by tenant+event-type) while still providing SIG/CAIQ evidence that the deletion actually occurred and that other logs remain intact.

Can Redwood propose a controlled workflow that: 1) allows per-tenant/per-event deletion within 7 days, 2) provides a tamper-evident evidence bundle (exportable CSV + hash + internal audit record), and 3) documents where SOC 2 / SIG evidence lives for this flow?

We have a tight window — procurement needs this documented before June 8 for our contract.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Rogers
Security Programs Lead — Aurabox Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Rogers <tim.rogers@aurabox.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Granular deletion exception for short-lived audit records / SIG artifacts

Tim — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a tenant-scoped granular deletion workflow with evidence exports, but we want to align on the controls and operational steps so the evidence is cryptographically verifiable and auditable for SIG/C A I Q reviewers.

High-level proposal I quickly sketched:
- Retention buckets: 0–7d (candidate for deletion), 8–30d (forensics snapshot hold only by request).
- Deletion API: tenant-scoped, event-type filter, requires an authorized request signed by a customer admin + Redwoods ops approval for same-day requests.
- Evidence package: export of deleted row hashes, a signed deletion manifest (HMAC+timestamp), and a separate immutable audit record in our SOC2-logged system.

I'm looping Marcus (runtime) and Neha (compliance) to add technical and control detail. Attached: a draft mapping template (sig-evidence-mapping.xlsx) for what auditors typically want.

Would you and Legal be OK with an approach that keeps 0–7d deletions immediately eliminable, with a separate short-lived escrow if Aurabox asks for forensics beyond 7d? If so, Marcus will outline the exact retention/queries and Neha will map the evidence to SIG/C A I Q rows.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
Attachment: sig-evidence-mapping.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Timothy Rogers <tim.rogers@aurabox.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T20:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Granular deletion exception for short-lived audit records / SIG artifacts

Thanks — technical confirmation and proposed workflow below. Keeping this short and actionable.

What Redwood can do (runtime + data lifecycle):
1) Tagging: All session/audit rows produced by the serving runtime are tagged with tenant_id, event_type, source_shard, and a monotonic event_id.
2) Granular delete API: a DELETE endpoint that accepts tenant_id + event_type + time-window. Deletes operate in two phases: (a) logical tombstone (immediate), (b) physical prune during the next housekeeping window (within 24 hours).
3) Evidence generation: when a delete is requested we snapshot the set of affected event_ids, compute SHA256 for each row, produce a deletion_manifest.json (manifest includes requestor, approver, timestamp, affected_count, and the list of hashes). The manifest is signed by Redwood's KMS key and stored in our immutable audit store (SOC 2-backed).
4) Compensating control for 0–7d purge: optional short-term escrow — a one-time encrypted snapshot accessible only to authorized Aurabox contacts for up to 30 days (requires signed JIT approval).

Operational guardrails:
- Customer deletion requests require API-level auth and an email/portal approval from an authorized Aurabox admin (we can support DocuSign idempotent approval if Legal prefers).
- For SIG/C A I Q evidence mapping: Neha will populate the spreadsheet with the exact control IDs and the sample artifacts (manifest example, signed export, audit-log reference).

Attached: proposed-deletion-workflow.md (contains sample manifest and housekeeping schedule).

Let me know if you need the deletion manifest to include per-row schemas or redacted payloads (we can include both hash-only and hash+sample payload modes).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-deletion-workflow.md

From: Timothy Rogers <tim.rogers@aurabox.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aurabox Legal <legal@aurabox.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Granular deletion exception for short-lived audit records / SIG artifacts

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail — this looks workable. A few follow-ups from Legal:
- Please include an example deletion_manifest (redacted rows ok) so auditors can validate the hash process.
- In the SIG mapping sheet, highlight which control IDs are satisfied by the signed manifest + immutable audit pointer (we usually reference the O365/DocuSign evidence style so auditors see the chain).
- Aurabox requests the short-term escrow option be documented as "customer-requested forensics snapshot" and require an emailed approval + ticket id; we'll provide a named approver list.

If you can drop the example manifest and an updated sig-evidence-mapping.xlsx by EOD Friday (June 1), procurement will be able to accept the deviation and finalize contract language.

I'll loop Legal and ops to provide the approver list. Thanks again.

-Tim
Timothy Rogers
Security Programs Lead — Aurabox Health
